title: Time Slip Theatre 'Frozen' in Louisville, Dec. 4-20 | Queer Kentucky
site_name: Queer Kentucky | Kentucky's Only LGBTQ+ Newsroom
excerpt: Time Slip Theatre stages Disney's "Frozen" The Broadway Musical Dec. 4-20 at 100 W. Ormsby Ave. in Old Louisville, with a winter village on the patio. Tickets from $28.
content:
Time Slip Theatre, a 501(c)(3) theatre company most known for its productions of “The Rocky Horror Show,” is excited to present its biggest show yet: Disney’s “Frozen” The Broadway Musical.

Inspired by Disney’s landmark 2013 film, “Frozen” follows two princess sisters in the Kingdom of Arendelle. The older sister, Elsa, was born with magical powers that she tries earnestly to hide as she approaches the day she becomes queen. Meanwhile Anna, the younger sister, is full of hope, optimism and excitement for possibility. But when Elsa loses control of her powers, the kingdom is thrown into a ferocious winter storm of ice that only an act of true love can thaw. Featuring such iconic songs as “Let It Go,” “For the First Time in Forever,” “Do You Want to Build a Snowman?” and more, FROZEN is irresistible for the whole family and proves that kindness, empathy and love can be the most magical gifts of all.

Directed by Remy Sisk, the show will run December 4-20 at Time Slip Theatre in Old Louisville, 100 W. Ormsby Ave, and will be the first mainstage show in the sanctuary space. All shows except Sundays are at 7 p.m., with Sundays at 5:30 p.m. Doors open 30 minutes prior to showtime and the show runs 2 hours 30 minutes with one intermission. Tickets start at $28 and are available here.

Time Slip will also be transforming its outdoor back patio space into an outdoor winter village, making it a holiday destination for the whole family with more to explore beyond the stage show.

“While Time Slip has been ambitious with its material in the past, nothing compares to Disney’s ‘Frozen’!” said Time Slip Artistic Director and director of “Frozen,” Remy Sisk. “Bringing this massive spectacle to the stage is certainly exciting. But in addition to the magic, I’m looking forward to seeing the emotional resonance and truth that is at the heart of it play out on stage. ‘Frozen,’ though fantastical, is also such a human story, and the intersection of Disney magic and authentic emotionalism is a really beautiful one, especially at this time of year.”

“Frozen” is the second show of Time Slip’s 2026-27 season and will be followed by an interactive production of “The Yellow Wallpaper” in March, and “Ride the Cyclone” in May.

This announcement was provided by Time Slip Theatre.
